name: Average Return Calculator
meta_title: Average Return Calculator: Arithmetic vs. Geometric (CAGR)
meta_description: Find the arithmetic and geometric average (CAGR) of yearly investment returns, plus the money-weighted return on an account with deposits and withdrawals.
subtitle: Compare the simple (arithmetic) average of your yearly returns with the compound (geometric) average, or work out the money-weighted return on an account you added to and withdrew from.

The geometric average is the steady yearly rate that turns your starting amount into the same ending value. The arithmetic average is a simple mean of the yearly figures and is higher whenever returns go up and down.

The annualized figure is the rate that makes all the money in and out balance on a 365-day year (the same method as a spreadsheet's XIRR). The whole-period figure uses the Modified Dietz method.
